comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body:
## Third confirmed occurrence — and it settles the fix direction

Reproduced again, independently, closing `electronic-deducible-maggot`. Two edges to the same
target, distinguishable by link id:

- `8b828d0a` — written earlier by `rebar link <bug> <origin> caused_by`
- `93b33884` — written by the close's `--caused-by`

`rebar unlink <bug> <origin> caused_by` removed **precisely one**, leaving one. That is now 3/3
reproductions and 3/3 successful repairs, so both the trigger and the remedy are reliable.

## The important part: passing the flag is still CORRECT

The tempting reading of this bug is "stop passing `--caused-by` when a link already exists." That
would be wrong, and this occurrence demonstrates why concretely.

Had the close been made with an EMPTY `--caused-by`, blame auto-derivation would have run
unconditionally and named a **June file-move carrier in `test_cli.py`** — a file whose lines
predate the behaviour change entirely. The proven origin is `8d36-a15a-fcbd-4ebd`, reached through
the unmet-obligation path: a later change altered test-distribution assumptions without updating
the tests that relied on the marker. Blame cannot find that, by construction.

So the two failure modes are NOT symmetric:

| | edge written | metric effect |
|---|---|---|
| pass the flag with an existing link | duplicate, **correct** target | one escape counted twice |
| omit the flag | **wrong** target, silently | one escape charged to an innocent ticket |

A duplicate correct edge is recoverable and visibly wrong. A single wrong edge is neither — it
looks exactly like a considered attribution. **The guidance to always pass the flag should stand;
the defect is that the write is not idempotent.**

That resolves the "Direction" section's open question in favour of making the `--caused-by` write
idempotent for an identical `(relation, target)` pair, and against the alternative remedy of
amending the `/rebar-debug` guidance to stop prescribing the combination. Amending the guidance
would trade a clean invariant for a rule agents must remember, AND would reintroduce the
strictly worse wrong-edge failure mode.

## Corroborating pattern

This is the fourth attribution today to resolve as an unmet obligation where naive blame would
have named the wrong ticket (the others: `fc20` for the disposition gate, `789c` for the dedup
consumer, `c1de` for the write-path drain gate). In every one, the fix site was not the cause site.
That is the exact case the escape metric most needs to get right, and the case where an empty
`--caused-by` is most dangerous — which is why the duplicate is the cheaper of the two failures to
tolerate while this is unfixed.

Evidence supplied by the agent that closed `electronic-deducible-maggot`; it flagged rather than
wrote, since another ticket's RCA is outside its pre-approved writebacks.

comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body:
## Fixed — change 1973

### Where the non-dedup lives

**The close path specifically, not `rebar link`.** `add_dependency` (what `rebar link` calls)
already dedups: it returns an idempotent no-op when `_is_active_link(source, target, relation)`
is true. `_apply_caused_by` in `src/rebar/_commands/transition_close.py` deliberately routes
around `add_dependency` and writes through the lower-level `graph._links._write_link_event`,
because `add_dependency` REJECTS a closed source and the bug is already `closed` when the edge
is drawn. Bypassing the closed-source guard also bypassed the idempotency check sitting beside
it — that is the whole defect. Confirmed at runtime: the RED run produced two `caused_by`
entries with the same `target_id` and distinct `link_uuid`s.

Scope held: no blanket dedup across relations. `rebar link` is untouched.

### The AC3 decision — REPLACE, and why not "fail loudly"

A different origin passed via `--caused-by` when one is recorded now **replaces** the recorded
edge (unlink, then link). "Fail loudly" was considered and rejected on structural grounds:
`_apply_caused_by` is best-effort by construction — the close has ALREADY committed when it
runs, and every exception inside it is swallowed to a `logger.warning` so the close stands. A
raise there cannot reach the caller, so "fail loudly" would in practice be "fail silently", the
exact failure mode the AC exists to forbid. Replacement also matches the semantics: an explicit
flag is a deliberate, corrected attribution, and locking in a known-wrong origin is worse than
overwriting a superseded one.

The cases now:

| flag | recorded edge | result |
|---|---|---|
| explicit, same target | yes | true no-op — `link_uuid` preserved |
| explicit, different target | yes | replaced |
| empty | yes | blame does NOT run — no guessed edge beside a proven one |
| empty | none | blame runs, unchanged |

### RED -> GREEN -> mutation

RED first, for the right reason: 3 of 5 tests failed with a duplicated target in `deps`; the
anti-regression test (empty flag, no existing edge, blame must still run) passed before AND
after, so blame was never disabled.

Four mutations, all killed after one strengthening pass:

- drop the `culprit in existing` guard — **initially SURVIVED**: the replace loop unlinked and
  rewrote the identical edge, still leaving exactly one. Functionally one edge, but it churned
  the store and discarded the original `link_uuid`. Test strengthened to assert the recorded
  `link_uuid` survives the close — the real no-op property — and the mutant now dies.
- let blame run beside an existing edge — RED.
- drop the replace (unlink) loop — RED.
- disable blame entirely — RED (anti-regression test catches it).

### AC4

`metrics.bug_trends._derive_caused_by_fan_in` tallies **edges**, not distinct targets, so a
duplicate genuinely double-charged one origin. Pinned by a test asserting
`caused_by_fan_in(repo) == {origin: 1}` after the link-then-flag reproduction.

### caused_by: `555e-3efa-4ad6-4169`

Date test applied, and it does NOT resolve to the file being edited by accident — the cause
site IS the fix site here, on evidence. `add_dependency`'s idempotency guard predates commit
`0f99986` (2026-07-19, ticket 555e), which introduced `_apply_caused_by` and its direct-writer
path. 555e's own commit message documents bypassing the closed-source guard; it did not notice
it was also bypassing the idempotency check next to it. An unmet obligation on the new write
path, not a carrier commit.

### Gates

`make lint`, `make typecheck`, `check_complexity_baseline.py --check`
(`active=49 new=0 increased=0 stale=0`) all pass. 699 related tests green
(`tests/interfaces/lifecycle/`, `tests/unit/metrics/`, `test_transition_close.py`,
`test_epic_bug_screen_4b54.py`, backfill scripts).

comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body:
## CORRECTION to this ticket's premise — the trigger is not `--caused-by`

I filed this as "close `--caused-by` adds a duplicate edge". **`rebar transition` has no
`--caused-by` flag**, and unknown flags are silently ignored — proven on a live ticket with no
mutation:

```
$ rebar transition major-specified-bream open open --definitely-not-a-real-flag
no change: 50e3-6d2a-0e7f-4e92 already open      # exit 0, no error
```

`rebar transition --help` lists only `--class`, `--reason`, `--force`, `--output`. Filed separately
as `brokendown-moonlit-kiskadee` (`0276-7eea-baf0-48e3`, P1), since the flag IS documented in
`docs/user-guide.md:194`, `docs/clone-guidance.md` and the `/rebar-debug` skill.

## The corrected mechanism

Every duplicate observed today was:

1. an edge written earlier by an explicit `rebar link <bug> <origin> caused_by`; **plus**
2. an edge written by **blame auto-derivation running on close** — which does not check whether a
   `caused_by` edge is already recorded.

The flag I believed was creating the second edge was inert throughout. So the defect is
**"blame auto-derivation adds an edge without reconciling against existing ones"**, and it is
triggered by the far more common sequence `rebar link` → close, with no flag involved at all.

That makes the bug **easier to hit than filed**: it needs only that someone recorded the origin
before closing, which the `/rebar-debug` protocol explicitly encourages ("it gets the finding down
before Phase 2 can be interrupted").

## The fix in review (change 1973) is still correct

`_apply_caused_by` is where the blame-derived culprit lands, so making it reconcile against
already-recorded edges fixes the real trigger, not just the imagined one. No rework needed on that
basis.

One consequence for **AC3** (a different origin must not be silently dropped): that path is
currently **unreachable from the CLI**, since nothing populates an explicit culprit there. It
remains reachable from the library/MCP seam (`_lib_writes.py:339` threads `caused_by=`), so the
criterion is still meaningful and worth keeping — but it should be tested at the library seam
rather than through a CLI flag that does not exist. Once `brokendown-moonlit-kiskadee` implements
the flag, the CLI path becomes reachable and that test covers it too.

## An honest note on the evidence in my earlier comment

My second comment argued the guidance to always pass the flag must stand, because an empty flag
lets blame attach a wrong edge. **The premise was right but the illustration was wrong**: since the
flag never worked, blame ran on all four closes anyway — and in every observed case it landed on
**the same origin the agent had proven by hand**. So today's data says blame was redundant here,
not wrong.

The argument for supplying a proven origin still holds on principle. It just is not supported by
the examples I gave, and I have corrected the related ticket
(`major-specified-bream`, `50e3-6d2a-0e7f-4e92`) which over-claimed on the same mistake.

comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body:
## Correction to the coordinator's correction: `--caused-by` IS live

The coordinator flagged that `rebar transition` has no `--caused-by` flag, and filed
`brokendown-moonlit-kiskadee` (`0276-7eea-baf0-48e3`, P1) on that basis. I tested it before
acting on it. **The flag works.** The P1 should be re-scoped.

### Direct evidence — the global `rebar` binary, blame structurally unable to interfere

Fresh temp store, `git init` with **zero commits** and no `file_impact`, so
`blame.derive_caused_by` cannot return anything:

```
$ rebar transition <bug> in_progress closed --class=regression --caused-by=<culprit>
transitioned 323c-a36f-ab61-4068: in_progress -> closed; unblocked: none

$ rebar show <bug>   # deps
[{"target_id": "8aef-feb0-07e6-46c1", "relation": "caused_by",
  "link_uuid": "d62f4e21-01a7-4c39-af92-103ae23dbcac"}]
```

The edge points at the culprit named on the flag. With no commits in the repo there is no
other mechanism that could have produced it. `_parse_flags` registers it explicitly
(`parser.add_argument("--caused-by", dest="caused_by", default="")`,
`src/rebar/_commands/transition.py:163`), and the pre-existing interface test
`tests/interfaces/lifecycle/test_caused_by_autoderive.py::test_explicit_caused_by_on_bug_close`
drives the flag through the CLI and passes.

### Why the original experiment misled

It used a **no-op** transition — `transition major-specified-bream open open` on an
already-open ticket. That returns `no change: … already open` at exit 0 from an early return,
before any close-path flag handling runs. And `_parse_flags` documents that unknown tokens are
**silently skipped by design**. So the experiment established only that an unknown flag is
ignored on a no-op transition; it never exercised a close, which is the only path where
`--caused-by` means anything.

### The half of the finding that IS real

`--caused-by` is genuinely absent from `rebar transition --help` (0 occurrences), while it IS
documented in `docs/user-guide.md:194`, `docs/clone-guidance.md`, and the `/rebar-debug` skill.
That is a real help-text gap and worth fixing — but it is a discoverability bug, not an inert
flag, so P1 looks too high once re-scoped.

### Consequences for this ticket

- **The original premise stands.** Duplicates were flag-plus-existing-link, as filed. The
  three reproductions are sound as recorded.
- **The fix is unchanged**, and would have been correct under either premise, since
  `_apply_caused_by` is where both the explicit culprit and the blame-derived one land.
- **AC3 is reachable from the CLI**, not library-only. My tests drive the library seam
  (`rebar.transition(..., caused_by=...)`), which is the same `_apply_caused_by` entry point;
  the CLI path over it is covered by the pre-existing interface test above.

comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body:
## WITHDRAWING my correction — this ticket's ORIGINAL premise was right

My previous comment claimed `rebar transition` has no `--caused-by` flag and that every duplicate
came from blame auto-derivation. **That was wrong.** A peer session challenged it, I verified, and
the flag is live:

- `_commands/transition.py:123-124,164` — `_parse_flags` parses and returns `--caused-by`.
- `tests/interfaces/lifecycle/test_caused_by_autoderive.py:33` drives it through the CLI and passes.
- Demonstrated in a fresh store with **zero commits and no `file_impact`**, where
  `blame.derive_caused_by` could not have produced anything — the edge still named the flag's
  culprit.

My experiment was invalid: I tested a **no-op** transition (`open open` on an already-open ticket),
which returns early before any close-path flag handling. It never exercised a close.

**So the original filing stands exactly as written**: passing `--caused-by` when an identical
`caused_by` edge already exists creates a second duplicate edge. The `rebar link` → close sequence
the protocol encourages is the trigger, and the flag is a genuine participant, not a bystander.

Also withdrawn: my claim that AC3's different-origin path is "unreachable from the CLI". It is
reachable — the flag reaches `_apply_caused_by` the same way the library seam does. No test
re-anchoring is needed.

The one thing that survives from my correction: `rebar transition --help` genuinely omits
`--caused-by`, because `_cli/help/transition.txt` and the help blob in `_commands/transition.py:65`
are two sources that drifted when commit `0f999860ad` updated only the latter. That is a
discoverability gap, now correctly scoped as `brokendown-moonlit-kiskadee`
(`0276-7eea-baf0-48e3`, P3) — and it is why I misread the flag as absent in the first place.

Apologies for the churn on this ticket. The fix in change 1973 was never affected.

compiled_state.description:
## Problem

`rebar transition <id> in_progress closed --caused-by=<origin>` **adds a `caused_by` edge without
checking whether an identical one already exists**, producing two distinct links to the same
target. Since `caused_by` feeds `rebar metrics`' escape-rate lenses and the epic-close `caused_by`
floor, a duplicated edge double-counts one escaped defect as two.

## Observed, twice, in one session

Both tickets had a `caused_by` link recorded earlier via `rebar link`, then were closed with the
same value passed explicitly as `--caused-by`:

```
irongrey-chubby-oxpecker  caused_by -> 789c-1251-fc21-4cf6   (x2)
perkish-balsamic-pupfish  caused_by -> fc20-2df1-426e-42ab   (x2)
```

Two DISTINCT links, same relation, same target:

```
link_uuid= 4ae0ef85-aa7b-4ec8-9678-9dda3ee24133  target= 789c-1251-fc21-4cf6
link_uuid= be724547-5b94-417a-8e2c-aa5b32d994ea  target= 789c-1251-fc21-4cf6
```

A survey of the whole store found **exactly these two** tickets with duplicate `caused_by` edges,
which is consistent with the trigger being rare in practice — most closes do one or the other, not
both.

## The part that makes this worth fixing rather than just avoiding

**The `/rebar-debug` protocol instructs you to do both things that combine to cause it.** From the
attribution step:

> Recording the link early with `rebar link <bug-id> <origin-id> caused_by` ... is fine and often
> useful — it gets the finding down before Phase 2 can be interrupted — but it does **not** stand in
> for the flag. A close with an empty `--caused-by` re-runs blame auto-derivation unconditionally;
> it does not check whether the ticket already carries a `caused_by` edge, so it will happily add a
> second, guessed edge *beside* your proven one. ... Pass the flag on the close every time.

That guidance is correct about the danger it names (an empty flag lets blame add a **wrong** edge),
and following it faithfully — link early, then always pass the flag — deterministically produces a
**duplicate** edge instead. The advice and the implementation together guarantee the defect for any
agent that follows the protocol properly. Both tickets above were closed by exactly that route.

So the duplicate is not a user error to be documented away; it is the protocol's prescribed path.

## Severity, stated honestly

Bounded. A duplicate edge points at the RIGHT origin, so it is strictly less harmful than the
wrong-edge case the guidance was written to prevent — nothing is mis-attributed. The harm is
double-counting in the metric, and `rebar unlink <source> <target> caused_by` repairs it after the
fact (used successfully on both tickets above, including on already-CLOSED tickets). Filed P2 on
that basis rather than higher.

## Reproduction

1. Claim a bug and confirm an origin ticket for it.
2. `rebar link <bug> <origin> caused_by`.
3. Close it: `rebar transition <bug> in_progress closed --class=<class> --caused-by=<origin>`.
4. `rebar show <bug>` — the `deps` list contains **two** `caused_by` entries with distinct
   `link_uuid`s and the same `target_id`.

## Direction (not a prescription)

Making the `--caused-by` write **idempotent** for an identical (relation, target) pair is the
obvious candidate and would leave every other path unchanged. Worth checking whether the same
non-dedup applies to `rebar link` generally, or only to the close path's write — the two have
different call sites and the fix may belong in only one of them. A blanket dedup across all
relations would be a larger behavioural change and is NOT proposed here: `relates_to` and
`discovered_from` may have legitimate reasons to permit repeats, and that question should be
answered on evidence rather than assumed.

If the code is left as-is, the alternative remedy is to correct the `/rebar-debug` guidance so it
stops prescribing the combination — but that trades a clean invariant for a rule agents must
remember, which is the weaker fix.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] Closing a bug with `--caused-by=<origin>` when an identical `caused_by` edge already exists
      leaves exactly ONE such edge — verified by a test driving the four-step reproduction above.
- [x] The protection the current guidance exists for is retained: closing with an EMPTY
      `--caused-by` must still not silently add a competing guessed edge beside an existing proven
      one — verified by a test.
- [x] A different origin passed via `--caused-by` when one is already recorded is NOT silently
      dropped: it either replaces the existing edge or fails loudly. Decide which and test it —
      silently ignoring a corrected attribution would be a worse bug than this one.
- [x] `rebar metrics`' escape-rate lens counts one escaped defect once for a ticket that went
      through the link-then-flag path — verified against the reproduction.
- [x] `make lint`, `make typecheck`, and `python scripts/check_complexity_baseline.py --check`
      (`new=0 increased=0 stale=0`) pass.

## Provenance

Found in live operation while closing `irongrey-chubby-oxpecker` and `perkish-balsamic-pupfish`
under `/rebar-debug`. Both were repaired with `rebar unlink` and now carry exactly one edge each, so
no metric is currently skewed by them.

file_impact.reason: The close path writes the --caused-by edge without deduping against an identical existing (relation, target) pair.
Candidate home for the caused_by application/dedup, depending on where _apply_caused_by resolves.
New test driving the link-then-close reproduction and the empty-flag protection that must be retained.
